meta.source: MATE ROV Competition: what the competition builds in students, inferred from the manuals
meta.year: not tied to a year; read from the 2024 to 2026 manuals
meta.scope_note: This is a cross-reference catalog, not a standard. MATE publishes no standards of its own, so each entry is this project's inference of what the competition requires, scores and explains, written so a teacher can see what has to be taught and where. It was built from the 2024 Ranger, 2025 Scout, Navigator and Ranger and 2026 Scout manuals and the 2027 Floats description. Scope: Scout, Navigator and Ranger. Point totals, electrical limits, depths and timings change by year and class, so none is recorded as a competency; class differences are noted under each entry and compared in mate-classes.json. MATE's own list of 18 skills is mate-skills.json and each competency names the ones it develops.
meta.codes_note: Each competency has an internal key (ENG, PRO or UND with a number) that keeps the data, links and lesson alignments stable; the keys are this project's, are not MATE's, and are not shown. On the pages the competencies are an outline: areas numbered 1 to 3 and items numbered within them (1.1, 1.2, ...) in this file's order, each with a very short phrase (the short field) for its bubble. MATE's 18 skills carry the visible codes (EMP.1 to EMP.9 and ROV.1 to ROV.9; see mate-skills.json).
meta.license_note: The competition manuals are (c) MATE ROV Competition under a Creative Commons Attribution NonCommercial NoDerivatives license, so nothing here copies their text; every entry is a paraphrase written for this project, with manual section names given as references only.

stated_aims.title: Skills for the workforce
stated_aims.text: The Overview opens by saying the competition develops technical talent and the skills employers want most: critical thinking, creativity, collaboration, time management and leadership, with data analytics, AI, machine learning and video marketing named alongside.

stated_aims.title: Eighteen named skills
stated_aims.text: Icons throughout the manual mark the 18 Evaluate-Compete skills, nine employability and nine ROV-specific, that each requirement helps develop.

stated_aims.title: Think like an entrepreneur
stated_aims.text: Teams are asked to act as a start-up company with named roles (chief executive, finance, regulatory affairs, research and development, systems engineering, testing, operations, fundraising and marketing, and an ESG analyst), and to build business acumen, make financial decisions from data, critique design solutions, and reflect on their own strengths and weaknesses.

stated_aims.title: The ocean we want
stated_aims.text: Each year frames the work with the UN Ocean Decade, with phrases such as moving from the ocean we have to the ocean we want, the client being us, and doing good for good, and tags every mission task with Ocean Decade challenges.
stated_aims.where: Overview and Request for Proposals, every manual

stated_aims.title: Real science each year
stated_aims.text: Every Context & Need teaches real ocean science and why it matters: ocean observing and cables (2024), Great Lakes acidification, invasive species, offshore energy and shipwreck heritage (2025), the cryosphere, cold-water corals, eDNA, whale entanglement, iceberg risk, hybrid energy and floats that avoid ice (2026).

stated_aims.title: Engineering reasoning
stated_aims.text: Judges want technical storytelling: evaluating alternatives, a work breakdown, constraints, a power budget, how sensors are calibrated, where code runs and how data flows, troubleshooting that is written down, and a project notebook.
stated_aims.where: Tips for effective written and oral communication, 2025 Ranger and 2026 Scout

stated_aims.title: Industry practice
stated_aims.text: Higher classes add practices from industry: a jobsite safety analysis with steps, hazards and safeguards in order of preference (Ranger), and scoring of teamwork, project management, problem solving and system design during the run (Navigator and Ranger).
stated_aims.where: Safety sections and scoring overview, 2025 Navigator and Ranger

stated_aims.title: Responsible use of AI
stated_aims.text: AI is welcome as a tool but not a crutch: describe how it was used, and do not use it to write the documentation or presentation.
stated_aims.where: Notes on the use of AI, 2026 Scout

stated_aims.title: The same kinds of task, every year
stated_aims.text: Tasks change yearly but come in families: recover objects, install or replace equipment, survey and measure, sample and analyze, and a separate device, the profiling float, which appears every year from 2024 to 2027 and gets harder.

stated_aims.title: What judges reward
stated_aims.text: Scoring rubrics rate each item from missing to exceeds, award extra for novelty, depth of understanding and analysis, effectiveness and quality of implementation, and deduct for relying on outside help or purchased parts.
stated_aims.where: MATE scoring rubric for technical documentation and engineering presentation

items.name: Turn a request for proposals into criteria and constraints
items.paraphrase: Read the mission request and the rules closely enough to say what the vehicle must do and what limits it, then decide what to build for the points available.
evidence: Context & Need and Request for Proposals (every manual)
Scoring overview (every manual)

items.name: Compare design alternatives and justify the choice
items.paraphrase: Come up with more than one way to solve a problem, compare them against the criteria, and explain why one was chosen, including whether to build or buy.
evidence: Tips for effective written and oral communication: evaluate competing alternatives, build versus buy (2025 Ranger, 2026 Scout)
Engineering presentation (every manual)

items.name: Budget power and protect against overcurrent
items.paraphrase: Measure what the motors and tools draw, size the protection to the real load, and stay inside the class's electrical limits.
evidence: Electrical specification sections, including fuse and current limits (every class)
Tips: how you arrived at your power budget
items.class_note: Current, voltage and fluid pressure limits are set per class and change; check the current manual.

items.name: Build reliable electrical and mechanical systems
items.paraphrase: Wire neatly, relieve strain where cables enter the vehicle and the control box, seal every connection against water, guard the propellers, and build a vehicle the crew can carry and launch by hand.
evidence: Safety and specification sections on wiring, strain relief, waterproofing and propellers (every class)
Safety inspectors' stated emphasis on workmanship (2026 Scout)

by_class.navigator: Hydraulic and pneumatic power is allowed within pressure limits, with its own diagram.

items.name: Design for the real environment and test under realistic conditions
items.paraphrase: Design for the conditions the vehicle will actually meet (conductive water, buoyancy and trim, interference, venue limits) and test there, because something that works at home may not work at the event.
evidence: Design and safety considerations (every manual)
Tips: what choices would matter in a less controlled environment

items.name: Control and operate a vehicle
items.paraphrase: Build a control system and pilot interface that turns what the pilot does into thruster and tool motion through the tether, with cameras and sensors as the class requires, and understand where the code runs and how data flows.
evidence: Control systems and command, control and communications specification sections
Tips: where code executes and the flow of data

by_class.navigator: Cameras are required to pilot, surface equipment may use AC power, and lasers are allowed with safety rules.

items.name: Sense, measure and calibrate
items.paraphrase: Choose sensors for the job, compare their readings against a trusted reference, and handle units and accuracy so the numbers can be believed.
evidence: Tips: how do you calibrate your sensors
Floats task: a benchmark temperature to compare against (2027)

items.name: Design and run a non-ROV device that works on its own
items.paraphrase: Build a second device, the profiling float, that goes down and comes back up independently of the ROV, gathers sensor data, and is run by hand or programmed to run itself.
evidence: Floats task in every class, every year from 2024 to 2027
Non-ROV device rules and design document
items.class_note: Demand rises by year: temperature only and propellers allowed in 2025, depth holding, a buoyancy engine bonus and transmitted data in 2027.

items.name: Collect, transmit, analyze and graph data
items.paraphrase: Gather measurements, get them from the device to a person, find what they say, and show it in a graph that answers a question.
evidence: Floats task graphing requirement (2024 to 2027)
Sample, survey and data-analysis tasks in 2025 and 2026
Tips: the flow and format of data

items.name: Do underwater work with purpose-built tools
items.paraphrase: Design and test the tools and techniques to recover objects, install or replace equipment, repair, release and survey, since the mission tasks are built from these every year.
evidence: Product demonstration tasks every year, 2024 to 2026

items.name: Test, troubleshoot and keep a record of what you learned
items.paraphrase: Test as you build, track down the real cause of a problem, and write down what happened, especially anything that takes a long time to solve.
evidence: Tips: record any problem that takes more than 20 minutes; project notebook

items.name: Trim and propel the vehicle
items.paraphrase: Design the vehicle so it floats level, holds its depth and moves where the pilot wants: set buoyancy and ballast, place thrusters, and match thrust to the job while keeping weight and cost in check.
evidence: Mechanical/Physical specifications: size, weight, sealing, propellers (every manual)
Propulsion and size limits every class works within
Floats task: buoyancy engine and depth hold (2025 to 2027)

items.name: Run the team as a company
items.paraphrase: Organize the team as a start-up with named roles, shared responsibility and a deck crew that works together.
evidence: Overview: think of yourselves as entrepreneurs, company roles (every manual)

items.name: Manage the project
items.paraphrase: Break the work into tasks, plan the schedule and budget, and meet the deadlines.
evidence: Tips: work breakdown structure; key deadlines
Organizational and operational effectiveness (Navigator, Ranger)

by_class.navigator: Organizational and operational effectiveness is scored, including project management.
by_class.ranger: Organizational and operational effectiveness is scored, including project management.

items.name: Communicate technical work in writing and in person
items.paraphrase: Tell the story of how the design was reasoned and tested in a spec sheet, technical documentation and an engineering presentation with questions, so a reader or judge new to it can follow.
evidence: Engineering and Communication: spec sheet, technical documentation, engineering presentation (every manual)
Tips: technical storytelling

by_class.navigator: The presentation is longer (15 minutes in the 2025 manual).
by_class.ranger: The presentation is longer (the Scout manual describes Ranger as 15 minutes).

items.name: Communicate with a non-technical audience
items.paraphrase: Present technical information so people outside the field understand it and care, in a display and in conversation with the public and the media.
evidence: Marketing display (every class)

items.name: Think like an entrepreneur
items.paraphrase: Use business sense: know your clients and products, make financial decisions from data, and take environmental, social and governance factors into account.
evidence: Overview: the entrepreneurial skill set, business acumen, ESG (every manual)

items.name: Work safely and manage hazards as industry does
items.paraphrase: Treat safety as the first rule: pass inspection, document the electrical system, wear protection, and think through hazards step by step before working.
evidence: Safety inspection and system interconnection diagram (every class)
Jobsite Safety and Environment Analysis and safety pre-inspection (Ranger)

by_class.ranger: A jobsite safety analysis (job steps, hazards, safeguards in order of preference, named responsibility) is required and scored, with pre-inspection documents and a company safety review.

items.name: Know and follow the rules and standards
items.paraphrase: Read every rule and ruling, ask questions in the proper form, and use the field's standard symbols and terms.
evidence: General and competition rules; the regulatory affairs role (every manual)

items.name: Use AI as a tool, not a crutch, and say how
items.paraphrase: Use AI to speed up work or fill gaps without letting it replace understanding, describe how it was used, and never use it to write the documentation or presentation.
evidence: Notes on the use of AI (2026 Scout manual)
items.class_note: Stated in the 2026 Scout manual; not in the 2024 or 2025 manuals read.

items.name: Give back to the community
items.paraphrase: Mentor newer teams, support local schools and share the work with the community and the media, and report the measurable difference it made.
evidence: Corporate responsibility (every class)

items.name: Ocean observing and data
items.paraphrase: Understand how floats, buoys, observatories, cables and maps collect the data that shows how the ocean is changing, and why that data should be open.
evidence: Context & Need: ocean observing, buoys, cables, floats (every year)
Ocean Decade tags 7 and 8

items.name: Ecosystems, biodiversity and invasive species
items.paraphrase: Understand coral and other ecosystems, why biodiversity matters, how invasive species are found and removed, and how eDNA reveals who lives in the water.
evidence: Context & Need: corals, eDNA, invasive carp and crabs, species near solar arrays
Ocean Decade tag 2

items.name: Climate and ocean change
items.paraphrase: Understand ocean warming, acidification, sea level and ice, and how carbon and heat move between the air and the ocean.
evidence: Context & Need: acidification, warming, the cryosphere
Ocean Decade tag 5

items.name: Ocean energy and the sustainable ocean economy
items.paraphrase: Understand offshore wind, solar and hybrid energy, what they cost and gain, how structures are kept from corroding, and how an ocean economy can be fair and sustainable.
evidence: Context & Need: offshore wind and solar, hybrid energy, corrosion
Ocean Decade tag 4

items.name: People, heritage and risk
items.paraphrase: Understand how ocean change affects people and what they value, such as shipwreck heritage, iceberg risk to platforms, whale entanglement in fishing gear and coastal resilience.
evidence: Context & Need: shipwreck heritage, icebergs, whale entanglement
Ocean Decade tags 2 and 6

items.name: Weigh environmental, social and governance factors in a decision
items.paraphrase: Weigh environmental, social and governance factors together when choosing what to build or do, with the question of how to move from the ocean we have to the ocean we want.
evidence: Overview: ESG, 'good for good', the ocean we have and the ocean we want; the 'client is us' (every manual)
